question: Dobutamine differs from dopamine in that

options.opa: It has good blood-brain barrier penetrability
options.opc: It does not activate adrenergic b receptors
options.opd: It does not activate peripheral dopaminergic receptors

analysis: Dobutamine and dopamine are both catecholamines, but they have different receptor affinities and effects. Dopamine activates both alpha and beta adrenergic receptors, as well as dopaminergic receptors. Dobutamine, on the other hand, primarily activates beta-1 adrenergic receptors with minimal effect on alpha or beta-2 receptors. This key difference leads to variations in their clinical effects.
